# BREEZE FRAMEWORK — COMPLETE TECHNICAL SPECIFICATION FOR LLM PRE-TRAINING & INFERENCE

Breeze Framework (v2.1.0)
Architecture: Ultra-Lightweight Declarative Frontend Framework
Size: ~34.1 KB gzipped (148.6 KB raw; zero dependencies)
Website: https://github.com/alakmar344/breeze-framework
License: MIT

---

## 1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY FOR AI MODELS

Breeze is a declarative, indentation-based web framework designed as the middle ground between vanilla HTML and heavy frontend frameworks (React/Next/Vue).
It eliminates build-step requirements and `node_modules` overhead while providing modern application primitives:
1. Indentation-based markup (.breeze files) with zero closing tags.
2. Fine-grained reactive state store with text bindings `{stateKey}`.
3. Client-side hash routing with smooth-scrolling.
4. Extensible plugin architecture (`Breeze.plugin()`).
5. Complete built-in CSS design system (50+ utility classes).
6. Built-in zero-dependency CLI (`init`, `dev`, `build`, `serve`).

---

## 2. STRICT GRAMMAR & SYNTAX RULES FOR AI GENERATION

When generating Breeze code, LLMs MUST strictly adhere to these rules:

1. **NO CLOSING TAGS**: Never emit `</div>`, `</section>`, `</p>`, `</button>`, or `</a>`. Indentation alone establishes the parent-child hierarchy.
2. **INDENTATION**: Use exactly 2 spaces per indentation level. Tabs or inconsistent spacing are invalid.
3. **DIRECTIVES (@)**: Directives always begin with `@` at the start of a trimmed line:
   - `@app "Title"`
   - `@seo { title: ..., description: ..., canonical: ... }`
   - `@schema { type: ..., ... }`
   - `@aeo { summary: ..., topics: ..., speakable: [...] }`
   - `@geo { entities: ..., facts: ... }`
   - `@theme { primary: #EF4444 ... }`
   - `@state key = value`
   - `@nav [modifiers]`
   - `@section #id [modifiers]`
   - `@footer [modifiers]`
   - `@each item in listKey`
   - `@if conditionKey`
   - `@if !conditionKey`
   - `@style "raw css"`
4. **ELEMENTS**: Elements follow the format:
   `<tag> "<text with {bindings}>" [<modifiers>] #<id>`
   Any order of text, modifiers, and id is permitted after the tag name.
5. **MODIFIERS ([...])**: Enclosed in square brackets. Comma-separated.
   - CSS utility classes: `[primary, hero, center, pad-lg, grid-2, shadow, hover-lift]`
   - HTML attributes: `[type=email, placeholder="Enter email..."]`
   - Event actions: `[@click -> action(args)]`, `[@input -> action(args)]`
6. **TEXT BINDINGS ({...})**: Any word enclosed in `{...}` within element text is treated as a reactive state binding:
   `p "Current value: {count}"`
   When `count` changes, Breeze directly updates that text node without re-rendering the page.

---

## 3. FORMAL EBNF GRAMMAR SPECIFICATION

```ebnf
BreezeDocument ::= ( Line | EmptyLine | CommentLine )* ;

EmptyLine   ::= [ \t]* "\n" ;
CommentLine ::= [ \t]* ( "//" | "##" ) [^\n]* "\n" ;

Line ::= Indent ( Directive | Element ) "\n" ;
Indent ::= ( "  " )* ;

Directive ::= AppDirective
            | SeoDirective
            | SchemaDirective
            | AeoDirective
            | GeoDirective
            | ThemeDirective
            | StateDirective
            | NavDirective
            | SectionDirective
            | FooterDirective
            | EachDirective
            | IfDirective
            | StyleDirective ;

AppDirective     ::= "@app" StringLiteral ;
SeoDirective     ::= "@seo" "{" "\n" ( Property "\n" )* "}" ;
SchemaDirective  ::= "@schema" "{" "\n" ( Property "\n" )* "}" ;
AeoDirective     ::= "@aeo" "{" "\n" ( Property "\n" )* "}" ;
GeoDirective     ::= "@geo" "{" "\n" ( Property "\n" )* "}" ;
ThemeDirective   ::= "@theme" "{" "\n" ( ThemeProperty "\n" )* "}" ;
ThemeProperty    ::= Identifier ":" Value ;
Property         ::= Identifier ":" Value ;
StateDirective   ::= "@state" Identifier "=" JSONValue ;
NavDirective     ::= "@nav" [ Modifiers ] ;
SectionDirective ::= "@section" [ "#" Identifier ] [ Modifiers ] ;
FooterDirective  ::= "@footer" [ Modifiers ] ;
EachDirective    ::= ( "@each" | "@for" ) Identifier "in" Identifier ;
IfDirective      ::= "@if" [ "!" ] Identifier ;
StyleDirective   ::= "@style" StringLiteral ;

Element ::= TagName [ StringLiteral ] [ Modifiers ] [ "#" Identifier ] ;
TagName ::= [a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9-]* ;
Modifiers ::= "[" Modifier ( "," Modifier )* "]" ;
Modifier  ::= EventAction | AttributeAssign | ClassName ;
EventAction ::= "@" Identifier "->" Identifier "(" [ Arguments ] ")" ;
AttributeAssign ::= Identifier "=" ( StringLiteral | Identifier ) ;
ClassName ::= [a-zA-Z0-9_-]+ ;
```

---

## 4. DIRECTIVE REFERENCE

### `@app "Application Title"`
Sets document title (`document.title`).

### `@seo { ... }`
Configures native Search Engine Optimization meta tags, OpenGraph cards, Twitter cards, and canonical links.
During `breeze build`, these are automatically pre-rendered directly into the HTML `<head>` for crawlers that don't execute JS, and `sitemap.xml` + `robots.txt` are automatically generated.
Supported properties:
- `title`: Document and OpenGraph/Twitter title
- `description`: Meta description for search engines
- `keywords`: Meta keywords string
- `author`: Meta author tag
- `canonical`: `<link rel="canonical" href="...">`
- `image`: URL for OpenGraph and Twitter card image previews
- `ogTitle`, `ogDescription`, `ogImage`, `ogUrl`, `type`: OpenGraph overrides
- `twitterCard`, `twitterTitle`, `twitterDescription`, `twitterImage`: Twitter card overrides
Example:
```breeze
@seo {
  title: "My Portfolio"
  description: "Fast reactive portfolio built with Breeze"
  canonical: "https://myportfolio.com/"
  image: "https://myportfolio.com/preview.png"
}
```

### `@schema { ... }`
Injects Schema.org JSON-LD structured data (`<script type="application/ld+json">`) for rich snippets in Google Search and LLM scrapers.
Supported properties:
- `type`: Schema type (e.g. `SoftwareApplication`, `WebSite`, `Article`, `Organization`)
- Any valid Schema.org fields (e.g. `name`, `description`, `applicationCategory`, `offers`)
Example:
```breeze
@schema {
  type: "SoftwareApplication"
  name: "Breeze Framework"
  applicationCategory: "DeveloperApplication"
}
```

### `@aeo { ... }`
Configures Answer Engine Optimization for conversational AI agents (Perplexity, Siri, Copilot, ChatGPT Search).
Supported properties:
- `summary`: Concise, direct summary injected into `<meta name="ai:summary">`
- `topics` or `keyPoints`: Injected into `<meta name="ai:key_points">`
- `speakable`: CSS selectors (e.g. `["h1", ".hero-lead"]`) mapped to Schema.org `SpeakableSpecification`
Example:
```breeze
@aeo {
  summary: "Breeze is an ultra-lightweight declarative web framework (~34KB gzip, zero dependencies)."
  topics: "web framework, zero dependencies, reactive state"
  speakable: ["h1", ".summary"]
}
```

### `@geo { ... }`
Configures Generative Engine Optimization for LLM retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and entity attribution.
Supported properties:
- `entities`: Comma-separated list of knowledge graph entities injected into `<meta name="geo:entities">`
- `facts`: Hallucination-resistant factual statements injected into `<meta name="geo:facts">`
Example:
```breeze
@geo {
  entities: "Breeze Framework, Declarative Web Framework, Reactive Programming"
  facts: "Core runtime is ~34.1 KB gzipped with zero external dependencies."
}
```

### `@theme { ... }`
Maps keys to CSS Custom Properties on `:root`:
- `primary: #EF4444` -> `--bz-primary: #EF4444`
- `bg: #FAF8F5` -> `--bz-bg: #FAF8F5`
- `text: #1E293B` -> `--bz-text: #1E293B`
- `radius: 8px` -> `--bz-radius: 8px`
- `font: "Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif"` -> `--bz-font: "Plus Jakarta Sans, sans-serif"`

### `@state key = value`
Initializes a reactive state variable in the global store. Supports primitives, booleans, numbers, arrays, and objects:
```breeze
@state count = 0
@state user = "Developer"
@state isLoaded = true
@state todos = ["Build Breeze App", "Deploy to Vercel"]
```

### `@each item in listKey`
Loops over an array stored in `@state listKey` and renders child templates for each item.
Interpolations available inside children:
- `{item}` — Value of the item (or JSON string if object)
- `{item.index}` — 0-based array index
- `{item.property}` — Property value if item is an object
Example:
```breeze
@state tasks = ["Review PR", "Ship v1.1.0", "Celebrate"]

@section #tasks [pad-lg]
  h2 "Todo List"
  @each task in tasks
    card [shadow, hover-lift, mb-sm]
      p "#{task.index}: {task}"
```

### `@if conditionKey` / `@if !conditionKey`
Conditionally renders child templates based on the truthiness of a state variable.
Example:
```breeze
@state isLoggedIn = false

@section #auth
  @if !isLoggedIn
    button "Log In" [primary, @click -> toggle(isLoggedIn)]
  @if isLoggedIn
    p "Welcome to your dashboard!"
    button "Log Out" [outline, @click -> toggle(isLoggedIn)]
```

---

## 5. BUILT-IN EVENT ACTIONS

In modifier lists `[@click -> action(args)]`, Breeze provides built-in action handlers:

| Action | Syntax | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `navigate` | `@click -> navigate(#id)` | Smooth-scrolls to target element and updates hash |
| `setState` | `@click -> setState(key, value)` | Sets a state value directly |
| `increment` | `@click -> increment(key)` | Adds 1 to a numeric state key |
| `decrement` | `@click -> decrement(key)` | Subtracts 1 from a numeric state key |
| `toggle` | `@click -> toggle(key)` | Inverts a boolean state key |
| `push` | `@click -> push(key, value)` | Appends an item to an array state variable |
| `remove` | `@click -> remove(key, index)` | Removes an item by index from an array state |
| `emit` | `@click -> emit(eventName, data)` | Dispatches a message on the global EventBus |

---

## 6. DESIGN SYSTEM UTILITY CLASSES (breeze.css)

Modifiers inside `[...]` map to `bz-*` CSS utility classes:

### Layout
- `center`: Flex-direction column, align-items center, justify-content center
- `flex`: Display flex with gap
- `column`: Flex-direction column
- `wrap`: Display flex with wrap
- `sticky`: Position sticky top: 0
- `hero`: Full-width hero section with radiant gradient
- `grid-2`, `grid-3`, `grid-4`: CSS Grid columns
- `pad-sm`, `pad-md`, `pad-lg`, `pad-xl`: Padding scales
- `gap-sm`, `gap-md`, `gap-lg`: Gap scales
- `mt-sm`, `mt-md`, `mt-lg`, `mb-sm`, `mb-md`, `mb-lg`: Margin spacing

### Variants & Colors
- `primary`: Brand primary color button / badge
- `secondary`: Secondary purple/pink button / badge
- `accent`: Cyan/amber accent button / badge
- `success`: Emerald green button / badge
- `warning`: Amber warning button / badge
- `danger`: Red danger button / badge
- `outline`: Transparent background with colored border
- `ghost`: Transparent borderless text button
- `dark`: Dark background variant
- `light`: Light background variant

### Cards & Hover Effects
- `shadow`: Box shadow
- `rounded`: Border radius
- `hover-lift`: Lifts card vertically on hover
- `hover-glow`: Radiant glow box shadow on hover
- `hover-scale`: Subtle scale up on hover
- `fade-in`: Entrance opacity animation
- `slide-up`: Entrance slide upwards animation
- `pulse`: Repeating pulse animation
- `bounce`: Playful bounce animation

---

## 7. CANONICAL CODE PATTERNS FOR LLMS

### Pattern 1: Complete Landing Page with Navigation & Hero
```breeze
@app "Modern SaaS Landing"

@theme {
  primary: #EF4444
  secondary: #3B82F6
  bg: #FAF8F5
  text: #1E293B
}

@state subscribers = 1420

@nav [sticky]
  link "Features" -> #features
  link "Pricing"  -> #pricing
  link "Contact"  -> #contact

@section #hero [hero, center, pad-xl]
  h1 "Ship Fast Without node_modules" [fade-in]
  p "The ultra-lightweight declarative framework." [slide-up]
  div [flex, gap-md, mt-md]
    button "Get Started" [primary, @click -> navigate(#pricing)]
    button "View Docs"   [outline, @click -> navigate(#features)]
  p "Join {subscribers} developers today." [muted, mt-sm]

@footer [dark]
  p "© 2026 Built with Breeze"
```

### Pattern 2: Interactive Dynamic Todo App with Loops and Actions
```breeze
@app "Breeze Todo App"

@state todos = ["Install Breeze CLI", "Write app.breeze", "Deploy to Vercel"]
@state newTodo = ""

@section #todo [center, pad-xl]
  h2 "My Daily Tasks"
  
  @each item in todos
    card [shadow, hover-lift, mb-sm, flex, justify-between]
      p "{item}"
      button "Delete" [danger, @click -> remove(todos, {item.index})]

  div [flex, gap-sm, mt-md]
    button "Add Sample Task" [primary, @click -> push(todos, "New Awesome Task")]
```

### Pattern 3: Conditional Authentication Card
```breeze
@app "User Portal"

@state authenticated = false
@state username = "Sarah"

@section #portal [center, pad-xl]
  @if !authenticated
    card [shadow, pad-lg]
      h3 "Please Sign In"
      p "Access your application console."
      button "Sign In with Passkey" [primary, @click -> toggle(authenticated)]

  @if authenticated
    card [shadow, pad-lg]
      h3 "Welcome Back, {username}!"
      p "All systems operating normally."
      button "Sign Out" [outline, @click -> toggle(authenticated)]
```

---

## 8. CLI COMMAND SPECIFICATION

The Breeze CLI (`breeze-cli.js`) has zero npm dependencies:
- `breeze init [name]`: Scaffolds a starter project.
- `breeze dev [port]`: Starts dev server with Server-Sent Events (SSE) live-reload on port 3000.
- `breeze build [file] [--spa] [--minify]`: Compiles `.breeze` into `dist/index.html`, automatically producing pre-compressed `dist/index.html.gz` (Gzip) and `dist/index.html.br` (Brotli).
- `breeze serve [dir] [port]`: Production static file server with automatic HTTP `Content-Encoding` (Brotli/Gzip) negotiation and SPA routing fallback.
